qns_content.text: A hydrogen atom absorbs a photon of energy 12.09 eV from the ground state. To which energy level does it jump? (Use \( E_n = -\frac{13.6}{n^2} \, \text{eV} \))
A nucleus has a binding energy of \( 175 \, \text{MeV} \) and mass number 25. What is its binding energy per nucleon?
Which of the following elements is NOT commonly used as a dopant in Si or Ge?

text_solutions: Common dopants for Si or Ge are pentavalent (As, P, Sb) or trivalent (B, In, Al). Carbon (tetravalent) is not used as a dopant since it does not alter carrier concentration significantly.

qns_content.text: A ball is thrown upwards at \( 35 \, \text{m/s} \) from a \( 45 \, \text{m} \) high tower. What is its velocity when it hits the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

Two parallel wires \( 0.03 \, \text{m} \) apart carry \( 8 \, \text{A} \) and \( 3 \, \text{A} \) in opposite directions. What is the force per unit length? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
A material with susceptibility \( \chi = 3 \times 10^{-4} \) has a relative permeability \( \mu_r \) of:
A magnetic dipole of moment \( 0.6 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is in a uniform field of \( 0.4 \, \text{T} \) at \( 60^\circ \). What is the torque on it?
A wheel with 6 spokes of 0.3 m each rotates at 40 rpm in a 0.6 T field. What is the induced emf?
The magnetic potential energy of a dipole with \( m = 0.3 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in a field \( B = 0.6 \, \text{T} \) at \( 45^\circ \) is:
A bar magnet with original \( m = 2.0 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is cut transversely into two equal parts. What is \( m \) of each part?

text_solutions:
When cut transversely, each part has half the original magnetic moment.

Given: \( m = 2.0 \, \text{A m}^2 \).

Each part: \( m' = \frac{2.0}{2} = 1.0 \, \text{A m}^2 \).

qns_content.text: An electron moves at \( 8 \times 10^6 \, \text{m/s} \) perpendicular to a field of \( 0.15 \, \text{T} \). What is the radius of its path? (Mass = \( 9.1 \times 10^{-31} \, \text{kg} \), charge = \( 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} \))
The dimensional formula of momentum is \( [M L T^{-1}] \). What is the dimensional formula of impulse?

text_solutions:
Impulse = Force × Time.

\( [F] = [M L T^{-2}] \), \( [t] = [T] \).

\( [Impulse] = [M L T^{-2}] [T] = [M L T^{-1}] \), same as momentum.

qns_content.text: A lift ascends with an acceleration of \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 3 \, \text{s} \), then moves at constant speed for \( 4 \, \text{s} \). If a ball is dropped from the lift \( 5 \, \text{s} \) after starting, how far does it fall in \( 1 \, \text{s} \) relative to the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

text_solutions:
Lift after 3 s: \( v = 2 \cdot 3 = 6 \, \text{m/s} \), \( y = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2 \cdot (3)^2 = 9 \, \text{m} \).

At 5 s: Constant speed for 2 s, \( y_{\text{total}} = 9 + 6 \cdot 2 = 21 \, \text{m} \), \( v_{\text{lift}} = 6 \, \text{m/s} \).

Ball dropped: Initial velocity = \( 6 \, \text{m/s} \) upward, \( y = 6 \cdot 1 - \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot (1)^2 = 6 - 5 = 1 \, \text{m} \) above drop point.

Lift moves \( 6 \, \text{m} \) up, so distance fallen relative to ground = \( 21 + 6 - (21 + 1) = 5 \, \text{m} \).

qns_content.text: Three capacitors \( 5 \, \text{pF} \), \( 10 \, \text{pF} \), and \( 20 \, \text{pF} \) are in parallel. What is the total capacitance?
A spring (\( k = 700 \, \text{N/m} \)) is compressed from \( 0.1 \, \text{m} \) to \( 0.15 \, \text{m} \). What is the work done by the spring force?
A charge of \( 4 \, \mu\text{C} \) is moved from infinity to a point where the potential is \( 250 \, \text{V} \). What is the work done?

text_solutions:
Work done = Potential energy = \( q V \).

\( W = 4 \times 10^{-6} \times 250 = 10^{-3} \, \text{J} = 1 \, \text{mJ} \).

qns_content.text: A \( 12 \, \text{V} \) battery with negligible internal resistance is connected to a \( 3 \, \Omega \) and \( 6 \, \Omega \) resistor in series. What is the power dissipated in the \( 6 \, \Omega \) resistor?
The dimensional formula of pressure gradient is \( [M L^{-2} T^{-2}] \). Which quantity shares the same dimensions?

A water sample of volume \( 2 \, \text{litres} \) is compressed by a pressure of \( 2.5 \times 10^6 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). If the bulk modulus of water is \( 2.2 \times 10^9 \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the change in volume?

Two cells of emf \( 4 \, \text{V} \) and \( 8 \, \text{V} \) with internal resistances \( 1 \, \Omega \) and \( 3 \, \Omega \) are connected in series with a \( 8 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the current through the circuit?

text_solutions:
Equivalent emf: \( \varepsilon_{\text{eq}} = 4 + 8 = 12 \, \text{V} \).

Total resistance: \( R_{\text{total}} = 1 + 3 + 8 = 12 \, \Omega \).

Current: \( I = \frac{\varepsilon_{\text{eq}}}{R_{\text{total}}} = \frac{12}{12} = 1 \, \text{A} \).

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a feature of electromagnetic waves in vacuum?

options.text: They are transverse waves with no material medium needed

text_solutions: Electromagnetic waves in vacuum are self-sustaining oscillations of electric and magnetic fields and do not require a material medium for propagation.

qns_content.text: A wire of length \( 15 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) has a resistance of \( 30 \, \Omega \). What is the resistivity of the material?

text_solutions:
Resistance: \( R = \frac{\rho l}{A} \).

Rearrange: \( \rho = \frac{R A}{l} \).

Substitute: \( \rho = \frac{30 \times 2 \times 10^{-6}}{15} = 4 \times 10^{-6} \, \Omega \text{m} \).

qns_content.text: A stone falls freely from a height of \( 19.6 \, \text{m} \). How long does it take to reach the ground? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

text_solutions:
For free fall, use \( y = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \).

Here, \( y = 19.6 \, \text{m} \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

Substitute: \( 19.6 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 9.8 \cdot t^2 \Rightarrow 19.6 = 4.9 t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 4 \Rightarrow t = 2 \, \text{s} \).

The time taken is \( 2 \, \text{s} \).

qns_content.text: A soap film supports \( 2.0 \times 10^{-2} \, \text{N} \) over a \( 40 \, \text{cm} \) slider. What is the surface tension?
Two cells in parallel have emf \( 10 \, \text{V} \) and \( 5 \, \text{V} \) with internal resistances \( 2 \, \Omega \) and \( 1 \, \Omega \). What is the equivalent internal resistance?
A satellite orbits a planet at \( 1.5 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \) from its center with a period of 4 hours. What is the planet’s mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))

An aluminium block of dimensions \( 0.4 \, \text{m} \times 0.3 \, \text{m} \times 0.1 \, \text{m} \) is subjected to a shearing force of \( 4 \times 10^4 \, \text{N} \). If the shear modulus of aluminium is \( 2.5 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the shear strain?

text_solutions:
Shear modulus: \( G = \frac{\text{Shear stress}}{\text{Shear strain}} \).

Shear stress: \( \text{Shear stress} = \frac{F}{A} \), \( A = 0.4 \times 0.3 = 0.12 \, \text{m}^2 \).

Shear stress: \( \frac{4 \times 10^4}{0.12} \approx 3.33 \times 10^5 \, \text{N/m}^2 \).

Shear strain: \( \text{Shear strain} = \frac{\text{Shear stress}}{G} = \frac{3.33 \times 10^5}{2.5 \times 10^{10}} \approx 1.33 \times 10^{-5} \).

qns_content.text: A \( 80 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the inductive reactance?

A \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) block on a \( 37^\circ \) incline (\( \mu_s = 0.5 \)) is pulled upward by a rope at \( 53^\circ \) to the incline with just enough force to start motion. What is the tension? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \sin 37^\circ = 0.6 \), \( \cos 37^\circ = 0.8 \), \( \sin 53^\circ = 0.8 \), \( \cos 53^\circ = 0.6 \))

A gas at \( 2.5 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 57^\circ \text{C} \) occupies \( 10 \, \text{L} \). If the volume is reduced to \( 6 \, \text{L} \) and temperature drops to \( 7^\circ \text{C} \), what is the final pressure?
A stone is thrown horizontally at \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) from a height of \( 19.6 \, \text{m} \). How much time does it take to reach the ground? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

text_solutions:
Vertical motion: \( y = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \), where \( y = -19.6 \, \text{m} \).

\( -19.6 = \frac{1}{2} \times 9.8 \times t^2 \Rightarrow -19.6 = 4.9 t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 4 \Rightarrow t = 2 \, \text{s} \).

qns_content.text: A solid has a molar specific heat capacity of \( 26.5 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \). Which element could it be?
The mean free path of a gas is \(3 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\) at a certain temperature. If the temperature is halved at constant pressure, what is the new mean free path?

text_solutions:
\(l \propto \frac{1}{n}\), \(n \propto \frac{P}{T}\). At constant \(P\), \(n \propto \frac{1}{T}\).

If \(T\) halved, \(n\) doubles, \(l\) halves.

New \(l = \frac{3 \times 10^{-7}}{2} = 1.5 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m} \).

qns_content.text: A \( 1100 \, \text{kg} \) car turns on a banked road (\( \theta = 20^\circ \), \( \mu_s = 0.15 \)) with radius \( 55 \, \text{m} \). What is the maximum speed without slipping? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \tan 20^\circ \approx 0.364 \))
What is the critical angle for a glass-air interface if the refractive index of glass is \( 1.52 \)?
In a single-slit diffraction pattern, what is the angular width of the central maximum if the slit width is \( 2.0 \, \mu\text{m} \) and the wavelength is \( 400 \, \text{nm} \)?
A spring-mass system has \( m = 1 \, \text{kg}, k = 400 \, \text{N/m} \). What is its frequency?
A \( 2 \, \text{kg} \) object moves with a velocity of \( 4 \, \text{m/s} \) along the x-axis. What is the velocity of its center of mass?

text_solutions:
For a single object, the velocity of the center of mass equals the velocity of the object.

Given: \( v = 4 \, \text{m/s} \) along x-axis.

Velocity of CM = \( 4 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} \, \text{m/s} \).

qns_content.text: A spring system has \( m = 0.1 \, \text{kg}, k = 40 \, \text{N/m}, A = 10 \, \text{cm} \). What is the kinetic energy at \( x = 5 \, \text{cm} \)?
A plane sheet has \( \sigma = 8.854 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{C/m}^2 \). What is the electric field near it?
A string vibrates with a stationary wave \( y = 0.1 \sin (\frac{2\pi x}{3}) \cos (150\pi t) \). What is the distance between a node and the next antinode?

A \( 2 \, \text{kg} \) mass is moved from \( 2 R_E \) to \( 4 R_E \) from Earth’s center. What is the change in potential energy? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
The threshold wavelength of a metal is \( 550 \, \text{nm} \). What is its work function in joules? (Take \( h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34} \, \text{J s} \), \( c = 3 \times 10^8 \, \text{m/s} \))

A \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) block on a horizontal surface (\( \mu_k = 0.2 \)) is pulled by a \( 8 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley. A \( 10 \, \text{N} \) force opposes the \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) block. What is the tension? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
What is the hybridization of the sulfur atom in \( \ce{SCl2} \)?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{SCl2} \), sulfur forms 2 bonds and has 2 lone pairs, requiring 4 hybrid orbitals, achieved by \( sp^3 \) hybridization.

qns_content.text: For the reaction \( \ce{N2(g) + 2O2(g) <=> 2NO2(g)} \), \( K_c = 0.04 \) at 500 K. If initial concentrations are \( [\ce{N2}] = 0.2 \) M and \( [\ce{O2}] = 0.3 \) M, what is \( [\ce{NO2}] \) at equilibrium?
What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2NH2} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 4-carbon chain with an -NH2 group on carbon 1. The parent chain is butane, and the suffix is -amine. The name is butan-1-amine.

qns_content.text: What is the degree of dissociation of 0.01 M acetic acid if its molar conductivity is 39.05 S cm² mol⁻¹ and \( \Lambda_m^0 = 390.5 \, \text{S cm}^2 \text{mol}^{-1} \)?

Which of the following transition metals is used in hydrogenation of fats?

text_solutions: Nickel (Ni) catalysts are used in the hydrogenation of fats to produce saturated fats.

qns_content.text: Which complex has a tetrahedral geometry?

text_solutions: \( \ce{[MnBr4]^{2-}} \) (Mn²⁺, 4 ligands) adopts tetrahedral geometry due to \( sp^3 \) hybridization with weak field \( \ce{Br^-} \), unlike the octahedral or square planar options.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a secondary alkyl halide?

text_solutions: In secondary alkyl halides, the halogen is attached to a carbon bonded to two other carbon atoms.

qns_content.text: The number of hydrogen bonds between adenine and thymine in DNA is:

text_solutions: Adenine pairs with thymine via two hydrogen bonds in DNA, contributing to the stability of the double helix.

qns_content.text: A solution is made by mixing 30 mL of methanol (\( \ce{CH3OH} \)) and 70 mL of water, with a total volume of 95 mL. What is the volume percentage of methanol? (Density of methanol = 0.792 g/mL)

text_solutions:
Volume % = \( \frac{\text{Volume of methanol}}{\text{Total volume}} \times 100 \).

Given volume of methanol = 30 mL, total volume = 95 mL.

Volume % = \( \frac{30}{95} \times 100 = 31.58\% \).

qns_content.text: A reaction has \( k = 6.0 \times 10^{-6} \, \ce{s^{-1}} \) at 300 K and \( E_a = 50 \, \ce{kJ mol^{-1}} \). What is the pre-exponential factor \( A \) in \( \ce{s^{-1}} \)? (R = 8.314 J/mol·K)
In combustion analysis, which gas is absorbed by \( \ce{KOH} \) to estimate carbon?

text_solutions: Carbon is converted to \( \ce{CO2} \) during combustion, which is absorbed by \( \ce{KOH} \) to form \( \ce{K2CO3} \), allowing carbon estimation.

qns_content.text: How many sigma bonds are present in the \( \ce{C2H2} \) molecule?

text_solutions: \( \ce{C2H2} \) has a triple bond (1 sigma, 2 pi) between carbons and 2 single bonds (2 sigma) to hydrogens. Total sigma bonds = 1 + 2 = 3.

qns_content.text: Which scientist first proposed that an atom is the ultimate indivisible particle of matter?

text_solutions: John Dalton, in 1808, proposed the atomic theory, considering the atom as the smallest indivisible unit of matter, explaining laws like conservation of mass.

qns_content.text: In the reaction \( \ce{2Al + 3Cl2 -> 2AlCl3} \), how many grams of AlCl₃ are produced from 13.5 g of Al and excess Cl₂? (Atomic masses: Al = 27, Cl = 35.5)

text_solutions:
Moles of Al = 13.5 / 27 = 0.5 mol.

2 mol Al produce 2 mol AlCl₃. Moles of AlCl₃ = 0.5 mol.

Molar mass of AlCl₃ = 27 + (3 × 35.5) = 133.5 g/mol.

Mass = 0.5 × 133.5 = 66.75 g.

qns_content.text: Calculate the heat required to raise the temperature of 54 g of water from 20°C to 40°C (specific heat of water = 4.18 J/g·K).
What is the pH of a 0.004 M \( \ce{Ca(OH)2} \) solution, assuming complete dissociation?
Which species acts as a self-indicator in redox titrations?

text_solutions: \( \ce{MnO4^-} \) changes from purple (+7) to colorless (+2) when reduced, acting as a self-indicator.

qns_content.text: What is the number of unpaired electrons in \( \ce{[FeF6]^{3-}} \)?

text_solutions: Fe³⁺ (\( d^5 \)) with weak field \( \ce{F^-} \) in an octahedral field is high spin (\( t_{2g}^3 e_g^2 \)), with 5 unpaired electrons.

qns_content.text: The chemical reactivity of Group 1 elements increases down the group due to:

text_solutions: Decreasing ionization enthalpy down Group 1 (e.g., Li to Cs) makes electron loss easier, increasing reactivity.

qns_content.text: What is the shape of the \( \ce{BeCl2} \) molecule according to VSEPR theory?

text_solutions: \( \ce{BeCl2} \) has 2 bonding pairs and no lone pairs around Be, leading to a linear shape (180° bond angle).

qns_content.text: What is the entropy change when a gas expands isothermally?

text_solutions: Isothermal expansion increases volume, increasing disorder, so \(\Delta S > 0\).

qns_content.text: Which compound exhibits functional isomerism with \( \ce{CH3CH2COOH} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2COOH} \) (propanoic acid) has the formula \( \ce{C3H6O2} \). \( \ce{HCOOCH2CH3} \) (ethyl formate, an ester) has the same formula but a different functional group.

qns_content.text: A solution of 12 g of a non-volatile solute in 100 g of water boils at 100.52°C at 1 atm. What is the molar mass of the solute? (\( K_b = 0.52 \, \text{K kg/mol} \))
What is the molar conductivity at infinite dilution for KCl if the ionic molar conductivities of K⁺ and Cl⁻ are 73.5 S cm² mol⁻¹ and 76.3 S cm² mol⁻¹ respectively?
For the reaction \( \ce{2A -> 3B + C} \), the rate of formation of B is \( 9.0 \times 10^{-4} \, \ce{mol L^{-1} s^{-1}} \). What is the rate of disappearance of A?
The maximum oxidation state of cobalt (Co, Z = 27) observed in its compounds is:

text_solutions: Co shows +2, +3, and +4, with +4 being the maximum (e.g., in \( \ce{CoO2} \)), though +3 is more common.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements is true about phenols?

text_solutions: Phenols are more acidic than alcohols due to the resonance stabilization of the phenoxide ion.

qns_content.text: What is the mass of 5 × 10²³ molecules of CH₄? (Molar mass = 16 g/mol, Avogadro number = 6 × 10²³)
Which model introduced the concept of discrete energy levels for electrons?

text_solutions: Niels Bohr’s model proposed that electrons occupy specific orbits with discrete energy levels, addressing Rutherford’s stability issue.

qns_content.text: Which method is used to purify a liquid organic compound that decomposes at its boiling point under normal pressure?

text_solutions: Distillation under reduced pressure lowers the boiling point, preventing decomposition of thermally unstable liquids (e.g., glycerol).

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements is correct about benzene?

text_solutions: Benzene is an aromatic compound with delocalized \( \pi \)-electrons, making it highly stable.

qns_content.text: Which compound reacts with Fehling’s solution to give a red precipitate?

text_solutions: Aldehydes reduce Fehling’s solution to give a red precipitate of \(\ce{Cu2O}\), while ketones do not.

qns_content.text: Which of the following elements is a chalcogen?

text_solutions: Chalcogens are Group 16 elements. Oxygen (O) belongs to this group, unlike F (Group 17), Na (Group 1), or Si (Group 14).

qns_content.text: What happens when propyne is treated with ammoniacal silver nitrate solution?

text_solutions: Terminal alkynes react with ammoniacal silver nitrate to form a white precipitate of silver acetylide.

qns_content.text: Calculate the freezing point depression of a solution made by dissolving 6 g of urea (\( \ce{NH2CONH2} \)) in 200 g of water. (\( K_f = 1.86 \, \text{K kg/mol}, \text{Molar mass of urea} = 60 \, \text{g/mol} \))
The product formed when \( \ce{KMnO4} \) oxidizes \( \ce{NO2^-} \) in acidic medium is:

text_solutions: \( \ce{5NO2^- + 2MnO4^- + 6H^+ -> 2Mn^{2+} + 5NO3^- + 3H2O} \). Nitrite (\( \ce{NO2^-} \)) is oxidized to nitrate (\( \ce{NO3^-} \)).

qns_content.text: Which compound is used as an industrial solvent and paint remover?

text_solutions: Dichloromethane (DCM) is widely used for these purposes.

qns_content.text: What is the correct IUPAC name of glycerol?

text_solutions: Glycerol is a trihydroxy compound and its IUPAC name is propane-1,2,3-triol.

qns_content.text: Which of the following compounds does not undergo nucleophilic addition reactions?

text_solutions: Carboxylic acids do not undergo nucleophilic addition reactions because the carbonyl carbon is less electrophilic due to resonance stabilization.

qns_content.text: Which of the following reactions confirms the presence of a primary aromatic amine?

text_solutions: Bromination with \( \ce{Br2} \) in water forms 2,4,6-tribromoaniline from aniline (\( \ce{C6H5NH2} \)), a specific test for primary aromatic amines due to the activating \( \ce{-NH2} \) group.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \) reacts with \( \ce{CH3CH2COCH3} \) followed by \( \ce{H2}/Ni \)?

text_solutions: Ethanamine reacts with butan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3CH2COCH3} \)) to form an imine, reduced by \( \ce{H2}/Ni \) to \( \ce{CH3CH2NHCH(CH3)CH2CH3} \) (N-(butan-2-yl)ethanamine).

qns_content.text: What is the geometry of the nitrogen atom in \( \ce{CH3NH3+} \)?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3NH3+} \), the conjugate acid of methylamine, nitrogen has four bonds (three to H, one to C) and no lone pair, resulting in a tetrahedral geometry.

qns_content.text: A compound has an empirical formula CH₂ and a molar mass of 70 g/mol. What is its molecular formula? (Atomic masses: C = 12, H = 1)

text_solutions:
Empirical mass = 12 + (2 × 1) = 14 g/mol.

n = 70 / 14 = 5.

Molecular formula = C₅H₁₀.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about fruits is incorrect?

options.text: Legumes do not split open at maturity
Aggregate fruits develop from multiple ovaries of a single flower

text_solutions: Legumes are dehiscent fruits that split open at maturity to release seeds.

qns_content.text: Which structure holds two chromatids of a chromosome together?

text_solutions: The centromere holds two chromatids of a chromosome together and provides attachment for spindle fibers during cell division.

qns_content.text: Which of the following occurs only in meiosis and not in mitosis?

text_solutions: Homologous chromosome pairing occurs only in meiosis during prophase I, leading to genetic recombination.

qns_content.text: Which group of plant growth regulators promotes cell division and cell enlargement?

text_solutions: Auxins and cytokinins synergistically promote cell division and enlargement, especially in tissue culture.

qns_content.text: Which of the following correctly describes linkage?

options.text: Linked genes are located on the same chromosome.
Linkage follows the Law of Independent Assortment.
Genes on different chromosomes are always linked.

text_solutions: Linked genes are located on the same chromosome and tend to be inherited together unless crossing over occurs.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about primary productivity is correct?

options.text: Primary productivity refers to the rate of energy capture by autotrophs.
Net primary productivity includes all the energy captured by producers.
Primary productivity is highest in deep ocean zones.
Gross primary productivity excludes energy lost in respiration.

text_solutions: Primary productivity measures the rate at which autotrophs capture and store energy as biomass.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is NOT a common pollination vector in flowering plants?

text_solutions: While wind, water, and insects are common vectors for pollen transfer, soil is not a pollination vector.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the xylem in vascular plants is incorrect?

options.text: Xylem vessels are dead at maturity and conduct water.
Xylem parenchyma stores food and helps in lateral transport.

text_solutions: Xylem primarily transports water and minerals, while phloem is responsible for transporting organic nutrients like sugars.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about placentation is incorrect?

text_solutions: Hibiscus exhibits axile placentation, not marginal placentation. Marginal placentation is found in pea.

qns_content.text: Which of the following taxonomic categories is the most general?

text_solutions: Kingdom is the broadest taxonomic category and includes the largest number of organisms.

qns_content.text: Which bacterial structure helps in attachment to host tissues?

text_solutions: Pili are small, bristle-like structures on the bacterial surface that help in attachment to host tissues.

qns_content.text: Which of the following occurs during anaphase of mitosis?

options.text: Sister chromatids separate and move toward opposite poles

text_solutions: During anaphase, sister chromatids separate at the centromere and are pulled toward opposite poles by spindle fibers.

qns_content.text: Which compound donates electrons to PSI in non-cyclic photophosphorylation?

text_solutions: Plastocyanin transfers electrons from the cytochrome b6f complex to PSI during non-cyclic photophosphorylation.

qns_content.text: Which parameter is used to measure growth in a pollen tube?

text_solutions: Growth in a pollen tube is measured by the increase in length as it extends toward the ovule.

qns_content.text: Which of the following correctly describes an exon?

options.text: Exons are only found in prokaryotic cells.

text_solutions: Exons are the coding regions of genes that remain in mRNA after splicing and are translated into proteins.

qns_content.text: Which of the following factors is most responsible for the regulation of population size in a natural ecosystem?

text_solutions: Predation plays a crucial role in regulating population size by preventing prey overpopulation and maintaining ecological balance.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a correct statement about habitat destruction?

options.text: Habitat destruction is a major cause of biodiversity loss.
Habitat destruction does not affect species survival.
Only aquatic species are affected by habitat destruction.
Protected areas like biosphere reserves cause habitat destruction.

text_solutions: Habitat destruction due to deforestation, urbanization, and industrialization is one of the leading causes of biodiversity loss.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about medullary rays in dicot stems is incorrect?

options.text: They are responsible for lateral conduction of nutrients.

text_solutions: Medullary rays are present in dicot stems and play a role in lateral conduction of nutrients.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about inflorescence is incorrect?

options.text: Cymose inflorescence has an acropetal flower arrangement
Umbel is a type of racemose inflorescence
Spadix is found in banana and maize
Capitulum is a type of racemose inflorescence

text_solutions: Cymose inflorescence has a basipetal arrangement, where older flowers are at the top and younger ones at the base.

qns_content.text: Why do dinoflagellates cause red tides in marine water?

text_solutions: Red tides occur when dinoflagellates, like Gonyaulax, undergo rapid multiplication, releasing toxins that affect marine life.

qns_content.text: Which organelle is involved in the formation of spindle fibers during cell division in animal cells?

text_solutions: The centrosome, containing centrioles, is involved in organizing spindle fibers during cell division in animal cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following best describes cytokinesis in plant cells?

text_solutions: In plant cells, cytokinesis occurs through the formation of a cell plate, which later develops into the cell wall.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about CAM (Crassulacean Acid Metabolism) plants is correct?

options.text: They open their stomata at night to reduce water loss.
They fix carbon dioxide only during the daytime.
They do not use PEP carboxylase for carbon fixation.
They perform photosynthesis only in mesophyll cells.

text_solutions: CAM plants open their stomata at night to prevent water loss while capturing CO₂.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an incorrect statement about the test cross?

options.text: A test cross is used to determine an organism’s genotype.
It involves crossing an individual of unknown genotype with a homozygous recessive individual.
A test cross always results in a 3:1 phenotypic ratio.
It helps determine whether a dominant phenotype is homozygous or heterozygous.

text_solutions: A test cross does not always result in a 3:1 ratio; it depends on whether the unknown genotype is homozygous or heterozygous.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about topoisomerase is correct?

options.text: It unwinds the DNA helix during replication.

text_solutions: Topoisomerase relieves supercoiling tension in DNA by cutting and rejoining DNA strands.

qns_content.text: Which genetic disorder is characterized by abnormal hemoglobin, leading to deformed red blood cells?

text_solutions: Sickle-cell anemia is caused by a mutation in the β-globin gene, resulting in deformed red blood cells.

qns_content.text: Which pollination type is most commonly associated with orchids?

text_solutions: Most orchids rely on entomophily, where insects act as pollinators, due to their specialized floral structures and scent.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about phloem fibers is incorrect?

options.text: Phloem fibers are the only dead component of phloem.
Phloem fibers are also called bast fibers.

text_solutions: Phloem fibers are usually dead at maturity and provide mechanical strength to the plant.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about stem modifications is incorrect?

options.text: Thorns in citrus plants are modified roots

text_solutions: Thorns in citrus plants are modified stems, not roots, and they provide protection against herbivores.

qns_content.text: Which of the following organisms lacks a true nucleus?

text_solutions: Bacteria are prokaryotic organisms and lack a well-defined nucleus.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements is true about lysosomes?

options.text: They are found only in prokaryotic cells.
They contain hydrolytic enzymes for intracellular digestion.

text_solutions: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes that break down cellular waste and pathogens through intracellular digestion.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about mitosis is incorrect?

options.text: Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells
Mitosis reduces the chromosome number by half
Mitosis is also known as equational division

text_solutions: Mitosis maintains the chromosome number and does not reduce it by half; that occurs in meiosis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of co-extinction?

options.text: Loss of a predator leading to an increase in prey population
Extinction of a host species leading to the extinction of its parasites
Introduction of an invasive species outcompeting natives

text_solutions: Co-extinction occurs when the extinction of one species leads to the extinction of another that depends on it, such as a host and its parasites.

qns_content.text: What is the primary reason for the loss of biodiversity in tropical rainforests?

text_solutions: Deforestation for agriculture, logging, and urban expansion is the major cause of biodiversity loss in tropical rainforests.

qns_content.text: Which genetic principle explains that different gene pairs assort independently of one another during gamete formation?

text_solutions: The Law of Independent Assortment states that different gene pairs segregate independently during gamete formation.

qns_content.text: Which enzyme is responsible for proofreading during DNA replication?

text_solutions: DNA polymerase has proofreading ability to correct errors during DNA replication.

qns_content.text: Which of the following pathways takes place in the absence of oxygen?

text_solutions: Glycolysis occurs in the absence of oxygen and is the first step of both aerobic and anaerobic respiration.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the chemiosmotic hypothesis is correct?

options.text: It explains ATP synthesis using a proton gradient.

text_solutions: The chemiosmotic hypothesis explains how ATP is generated due to a proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about venation is correct?

text_solutions: Monocots typically have parallel venation, where veins run parallel to each other, as seen in grasses.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about bryophytes is incorrect?

options.text: Bryophytes play a role in plant succession on bare rocks.
The male sex organ in bryophytes is called antheridium.
Bryophytes have a dominant sporophyte phase in their life cycle.
Mosses and liverworts are types of bryophytes.

text_solutions: The dominant phase in bryophytes is the gametophyte, not the sporophyte, which is dependent on it.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about oxidative phosphorylation is CORRECT?

options.text: It produces ATP using a proton gradient.

text_solutions: Oxidative phosphorylation occurs in the mitochondria and utilizes a proton gradient to synthesize ATP.

qns_content.text: What is the primary reason for genetic variation during sexual reproduction?

text_solutions: Crossing over during meiosis leads to genetic recombination and variation among offspring.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of euchromatin?

options.text: Contains repetitive DNA and does not participate in transcription

text_solutions: Euchromatin is loosely packed and transcriptionally active, allowing gene expression.

qns_content.text: Which factor influences the species-area relationship?

text_solutions: According to Alexander von Humboldt, species richness increases with the explored area, but only up to a limit.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about primary productivity is correct?

options.text: Gross primary productivity (GPP) includes energy lost in respiration
Net primary productivity (NPP) is always higher than GPP
Primary productivity is not influenced by environmental factors

text_solutions: Gross primary productivity (GPP) is the total energy captured by producers, including the energy lost during respiration.

qns_content.text: Which organ in frogs functions as both excretory and reproductive ducts in males?

text_solutions: In male frogs, the ureters act as urinogenital ducts, carrying both urine and sperm.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is NOT a function of the male accessory glands?

text_solutions: Testosterone is produced by the testes, whereas the male accessory glands secrete fluids that aid in sperm nourishment and transport.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements regarding population control is incorrect?

options.text: Encouraging early marriages is an effective method of population control.
Sex education plays a role in population control.

text_solutions: Encouraging early marriages does not help in population control; instead, it increases birth rates and related health risks.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements is correct about gene cloning?

options.text: Gene cloning produces identical copies of genes.
Gene cloning eliminates genes from the host genome.
Gene cloning is unrelated to recombinant DNA technology.
Gene cloning is used only for animal cells.

text_solutions: Gene cloning produces identical copies of a gene for research, medicine, and agriculture through recombinant DNA technology.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Panspermia proposes that life originated from Earth’s oceans.
Homo habilis is considered the first hominid to use fire.
Analogous organs have similar functions but different evolutionary origins.
Lamarck’s theory is widely accepted in modern evolutionary biology.

text_solutions: Analogous organs perform similar functions but have different evolutionary origins, such as wings of birds and insects.

qns_content.text: Which hormone inhibits the secretion of gastric acid?

text_solutions: Gastric inhibitory peptide (GIP) inhibits gastric acid secretion and slows down the digestive process.

qns_content.text: Which hormone regulates calcium levels in bones?

text_solutions: Parathyroid hormone regulates calcium levels by promoting bone resorption.

qns_content.text: Which heart chamber pumps oxygenated blood to the aorta?

text_solutions: The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta, which distributes it to the body.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about nucleotides is incorrect?

options.text: Nucleotides consist of a nitrogenous base, a sugar, and a phosphate group.
Nucleotides are the building blocks of nucleic acids.

text_solutions: DNA contains thymine instead of uracil. Uracil is found in RNA.

qns_content.text: Which of the following structures in birds reduces their body weight and facilitates flight?

text_solutions: Birds have hollow (pneumatic) bones, which reduce their body weight and aid in flight.

qns_content.text: What is the role of the collecting duct in the nephron?

text_solutions: The collecting duct plays a key role in concentrating urine by reabsorbing water.

qns_content.text: Which type of bonds does DNA ligase form while joining DNA fragments?

text_solutions: DNA ligase forms phosphodiester bonds between DNA fragments to create a continuous strand.

qns_content.text: Which toxic substance is released during the rupture of red blood cells in malaria?

text_solutions: Haemozoin, a toxic substance, is released when Plasmodium ruptures red blood cells, causing fever and chills.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Darwin’s finches are an example of convergent evolution.
Gene flow reduces genetic variation between populations.
Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium describes continuous changes in allele frequencies.

text_solutions: Gene flow, the exchange of genes between populations, reduces genetic differences and promotes homogeneity.

qns_content.text: What is the function of the zona pellucida in fertilization?

text_solutions: The zona pellucida is a glycoprotein layer surrounding the oocyte that facilitates sperm binding and, following fertilization, undergoes a cortical reaction to prevent polyspermy.

qns_content.text: Which type of bone cell is responsible for forming new bone tissue?

text_solutions: Osteoblasts are responsible for synthesizing and forming new bone tissue.

qns_content.text: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

options.text: Vital Capacity - Maximum air inhaled after forced expiration
Tidal Volume - Air remaining in lungs after forced expiration
Expiratory Reserve Volume - Maximum air inhaled after normal inspiration

text_solutions: Vital capacity is the maximum volume of air a person can breathe in after a forced expiration.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about enzyme inhibitors is correct?

options.text: Competitive inhibitors bind to the active site of the enzyme.
Non-competitive inhibitors bind to the active site of the enzyme.

text_solutions: Competitive inhibitors compete with the substrate for the active site, while non-competitive inhibitors bind elsewhere.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about sponges (Porifera) is correct?

options.text: Sponges possess a water canal system for filter-feeding

text_solutions: Sponges use a water canal system to filter food particles from water. They lack tissues and exhibit cellular-level organization.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements regarding respiratory diseases is correct?

options.text: Silicosis is an occupational disease caused by prolonged inhalation of dust.
Pneumonia is caused by exposure to silica particles.

text_solutions: Silicosis is a chronic lung disease caused by prolonged exposure to silica dust.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the hypothalamus is correct?

options.text: It directly generates motor impulses for voluntary movements.
It is not involved in endocrine regulation.
It does not play a role in maintaining homeostasis.

text_solutions: The hypothalamus regulates homeostatic functions such as body temperature, hunger, and hormonal balance.

qns_content.text: Which hormone is secreted by adipose tissue and helps regulate body weight?

text_solutions: Leptin, secreted by adipose tissue, signals the brain to reduce hunger and regulate body weight.

qns_content.text: Which nutrient in plant tissue culture media provides energy for cell growth?

text_solutions: Sucrose provides the energy required for the growth and development of plant cells in tissue culture media.

qns_content.text: Which type of cancer originates from connective tissues?

text_solutions: Sarcomas originate from connective tissues such as bones, cartilage, and muscles.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a key feature of the Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) program?

text_solutions: The RCH program aims to provide reproductive health education and promote awareness of contraception and maternal care.

qns_content.text: Which receptor mediates the rapid non-genomic actions of estrogen in target tissues?

text_solutions: Membrane-bound estrogen receptors mediate rapid, non-genomic effects of estrogen in various target tissues.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about enzyme inhibition is correct?

options.text: Competitive inhibitors bind to the active site of the enzyme.
Non-competitive inhibitors bind to the active site of the enzyme.

text_solutions: Competitive inhibitors compete with the substrate by binding to the active site, while non-competitive inhibitors bind elsewhere.

qns_content.text: Which sensory organ is well-developed in frogs for detecting vibrations in water and land?

text_solutions: The tympanum in frogs functions as an external ear and detects sound vibrations both in water and on land.

qns_content.text: Which class of vertebrates possesses a three-chambered heart with incomplete separation of ventricles?

text_solutions: Reptiles (except crocodiles) have a three-chambered heart with incomplete separation of ventricles.

qns_content.text: Which statement about the role of the renal pelvis is correct?

options.text: The renal pelvis is responsible for urine filtration.
The renal pelvis collects urine before passing it to the ureter.

text_solutions: The renal pelvis collects urine from the collecting ducts before it moves into the ureter.

qns_content.text: Which statement about synovial joints is correct?

text_solutions: Synovial joints have a fluid-filled synovial cavity that allows movement​.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about autoimmune diseases is correct?

options.text: Autoimmune diseases occur when the immune system attacks its own cells.
Autoimmune diseases are caused by bacterial infections.
Autoimmune diseases result from an external allergen.
Antibodies do not play any role in autoimmune diseases.

text_solutions: Autoimmune diseases arise when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body's own cells, leading to tissue damage.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about PCR is incorrect?

options.text: PCR is used to amplify DNA sequences.
PCR requires primers to initiate DNA synthesis.

text_solutions: PCR involves a series of temperature cycles, including denaturation, annealing, and extension.

qns_content.text: Which genetically modified plant contains the cryIAb gene for pest resistance?

text_solutions: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) corn contains the cryIAb gene, providing resistance to corn borers.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about transformation is correct?

options.text: Transformation is the uptake of foreign DNA by bacterial cells.
Transformation prevents the growth of bacterial cells.

text_solutions: Transformation allows bacterial cells to take up foreign DNA, either naturally or through artificial methods like electroporation.

qns_content.text: Which of the following diseases is caused by a fungal infection?

text_solutions: Ringworm is caused by fungal species such as Trichophyton and Microsporum.

qns_content.text: Which of the following best describes the function of the thalamus?

options.text: Relays sensory signals to the cerebral cortex

text_solutions: The thalamus acts as a relay center for sensory signals, directing them to the appropriate areas of the cerebral cortex.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about ATP is incorrect?

options.text: ATP is a nucleotide that stores energy.
ATP releases energy when a phosphate bond is broken.

text_solutions: ATP is a nucleotide, not a protein made of amino acids.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about cyclostomes is incorrect?

text_solutions: Cyclostomes (e.g., lampreys and hagfish) lack paired fins, unlike most vertebrates.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is correct about the function of white blood cells (WBCs)?

options.text: WBCs play a crucial role in immunity.
WBCs are the most abundant blood cells.

text_solutions: WBCs (leukocytes) are essential for immune defense against infections and foreign pathogens.

qns_content.text: Which of the following diseases is caused by a bacterial infection?

text_solutions: Typhoid is a bacterial disease caused by Salmonella typhi, which spreads through contaminated food and water.

qns_content.text: Which of the following enzymes is used to remove RNA during DNA isolation?

text_solutions: Ribonuclease (RNase) degrades RNA, allowing for the purification of DNA during isolation.

qns_content.text: Which nutrient is enhanced in Golden Rice through genetic modification?

text_solutions: Golden Rice is genetically modified to produce beta-carotene, a precursor of Vitamin A.

qns_content.text: Which phenomenon occurs when a population’s allele frequencies change due to random events?

text_solutions: Genetic drift causes random changes in allele frequencies, especially in small populations.
